Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh… –Matthew 19:6.

The marriage relationship was authored by God in the very beginning of time. God also offered to bless the marriage (Genesis 1:28) of the man and woman entering into it, if they desired to maintain its beauty and holiness. Since then, Satan has attempted, in every way possible, to corrupt and destroy the existence of Holy Matrimony. As early as Genesis 4:19, mankind was using polygamy to corrupt God's design of marriage. In Leviticus chapters 21 and 22, a plan, called a divorce, was put in place to legally dissolve the “first love”. This also included the option to remarry. When it was first developed as a practice, the call for divorce was initiated by man, not God, and was for the purpose of dissolving what was understood up until that time to be a lifelong commitment.

In this article we want to look at a number of points:

  • What does the Bible teach about marriage? Does the first marriage carry any special position with God?
  • What does the Bible teach about divorce? Does God recognize divorce as terminating the original marriage vow while either spouse is still living?
  • What does the Bible teach about the reuniting of a separated or divorced first marriage?

It is the desire of this study to be comprehensive, while allowing the scriptures to be their own interpreter, thus keeping commentary to a minimum. The purpose of this writing is to encourage diligence with prayer in seeking the will of God through a study of His Word. The desire of the writer has been to prayerfully consider all relevant scriptures and the context for which they were written.

What does the Bible teach about God's view of the first marriage?

At least five times in the Old Testament, the first marriage is described by the Lord as exclusive and lifelong. This same view was supported by Jesus and the apostles in the New Testament.

  1. Let thy fountain be blessed: and rejoice with the wife of thy youth –Proverbs 5:18. Note the attention given to the wife of thy youth.

  2. For the LORD hath called thee as a woman forsaken and grieved in spirit, and a wife of youth, when thou wast refused, saith thy God –Isaiah 54:6. Being a wife of one’s youth and then later refused, intensified the grieving of this forsaken woman.

  3. Yet ye say, Wherefore? Because the LORD hath been witness between thee and the wife of thy youth, against whom thou hast dealt treacherously: yet is she thy companion, and the wife of thy covenant. And did not he make one? Yet had he the residue of the spirit. And wherefore one? That he might seek a godly seed. Therefore take heed to your spirit, and let none deal treacherously against the wife of his youth. For the LORD, the God of Israel, saith that he hateth putting away: for one covereth violence with his garment, saith the LORD of hosts: therefore take heed to your spirit, that ye deal not treacherously. –Malachi 2:14-16. And why are they made one, exclusive to each other? To raise up a godly seed unto the Lord. Even though God hates putting away, men still try to cover it with a garment of civil, legal acceptance called "divorce".

  4. Matthew 19:3-12: V.4 In the beginning… Jesus, when asked by the Pharisees about this issue, takes them back to original intent of His Father when He chides them… And he answered and said unto them, Have ye not read, that he which made them at the beginning made them male and female –Matthew 19:4. He then goes on to remind them of the Scriptures teaching that …a man [shall] leave [his] father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they twain shall be one flesh? Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder –Matthew 19:5-6. Don't equate man’s authority (the civil court) with God’s authority when it comes to deciding what the facts are concerning marriage, divorce, and remarriage. We need to remember that it is God who has joined each marriage together in Heaven and has recorded them in the Book of Life.

  5. For the woman which hath an husband is bound by the law to her husband so long as he liveth; but if the husband be dead, she is loosed from the law of her husband. So then if, while her husband liveth, she be married to another man, she shall be called an adulteress: but if her husband be dead, she is free from that law; so that she is no adulteress, though she be married to another man –Romans 7:2-3. Again, this is pointing back to the beginning in order to establish a basis of Truth.

Only the death of either spouse will terminate the initial marriage covenant in the heavenly records. And once this life is over, only the heavenly records will matter—for all of eternity.

There are several exceptions to the Biblical ideal:

  • Defraud [deprive, keep back] ye not one the other, except it be with consent for a time, that ye may give yourselves to fasting and prayer; and come together again, that Satan tempt you not for your incontinency [lack of self-restraint] –1 Corinthians 7:5. So, restraining the marriage relationship for a time with voluntary consent from both husband and wife when there is a need for seeking God’s favor or guidance on a matter of great importance, may in some circumstances find God’s blessing. However, this should only be engaged in with a clear understanding and commitment by both spouses involved, about when and how to come together again, lest Satan tempt you. This exception has three clear qualifiers… 1) with consent, 2) for a time, & 3) for the purpose of giving yourselves to prayer and fasting.

  • And unto the married I command, yet not I, but the Lord, Let not the wife depart from her husband: But and if she depart, let her remain unmarried, or be reconciled to her husband: and let not the husband put away his wife –1 Corinthians 7:10-11. This is the Scriptural passage that frees the innocent spouse from biblical guilt when the other spouse is the one who chose to part ways. However, the teaching still remains that they shall not marry another “so long as the original partner remains alive”.

What does the Bible teach about God's view of divorce?

It hath been said, Whosoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorcement: But I say unto you, That whosoever shall put away his wife, saving for the cause of fornication, causeth her to commit adultery: and whosoever shall marry her that is divorced committeth adultery –Matthew 5:31-32. As Jesus taught the people in His Sermon on the Mount, one of the many things that He kept focusing on was this issue of God’s original plan for marriage.

“Saving for the cause of fornication” Fornication is any type of immorality prior to marriage. Modern-day Christianity, at times, struggles with this idea since the customs of the ancient Jewish culture have long since been forgotten. In Jewish culture, the betrothal period was considered almost as binding as the marriage ceremony itself, so much so that to end a betrothal required a “divorce”. With this as a foundational understanding, fornication here is speaking of immorality during the espousal or betrothal period. If any unfaithfulness was discovered, a writing of divorcement was required to break the betrothal, espousal, or engagement. This specific aspect of divorce was not criticized by Jesus. Even though they were not permitted to engage in the physical relationship of marriage during the betrothal period, they were still referred to as husband and wife. Finally, the reason this is referred to as fornication instead of adultery is because that during the betrothal period the marriage of the two has not yet taken place, nor has their relationship been consummated physically. Thus, just prior to the point in time when they are considered by God as being married, any outside relationship would be fornication, while just after they are considered married, any similar relationship would be adultery.

We have an excellent biblical example of this type of situation with Joseph & Mary in the following verses: Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost. Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily –Matthew 1:18, 19.

So, biblically speaking, divorce can put asunder the first marriage according to civil law but cannot terminate a first marriage before God. A divorced person remains the companion of their first marriage (as long as the other spouse is alive) even when remarrying, whether they are legally divorced or not, thus resulting in biblical adultery for both parties. However, when divorce is allowed to be recognized as being legitimate in breaking or annulling the initial marriage covenant, we have thereby removed the specific reason by which God calls subsequent marriages adultery.

In Matthew 19:3-10, Jesus is teaching the same lesson as in Matthew 5:31-32. However, Matthew 19:3-10 was initiated from an attempt by the Pharisees to trap Jesus with a question: They say unto him, Why did Moses then command to give a writing of divorcement, and to put her away? –Matthew 19:7. Jesus then responds further and says, …Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so –Matthew 19:8.

Also, in Mark it is written, But from the beginning of the creation God made them male and female. For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and cleave to his wife; And they twain shall be one flesh: so then they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder –Mark 10:6-9.

Thus, divorce, with all its regulations, is man's attempt to use civil law to terminate that which from the beginning was understood to be until the death of either spouse.

What does the Bible teach about the reuniting of a separated or a divorced first marriage?

He saith unto them, Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so –Matthew 19:8. Here Jesus is teaching the initial mind of His Father. In the law, Moses taught that… When a man hath taken a wife, and married her, and it come to pass that she find no favour in his eyes, because he hath found some uncleanness in her: then let him write her a bill of divorcement, and give it in her hand, and send her out of his house. And when she is departed out of his house, she may go and be another man's wife. And if the latter husband hate her, and write her a bill of divorcement, and giveth it in her hand, and sendeth her out of his house; or if the latter husband die, which took her to be his wife; Her former husband, which sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife… –Deuteronomy 24:1-4.

This is Moses' teaching regarding permission and qualifications for divorce which Jesus explained was because of the hardness of their hearts. Jesus further clarified this by saying, but from the beginning it was not so –Matthew 19:8.

Perhaps Jeremiah also is referring to Moses' writing in Deuteronomy 24:1-4 when he says, They say, If a man put away his wife, and she go from him, and become another man's, shall he return unto her again? shall not that land be greatly polluted? but thou hast played the harlot with many lovers; yet return again to me, saith the LORD –Jeremiah 3:1. The remainder of Jeremiah chapter 3 speaks of God receiving them back if they repent. God pleads for them to (v.13) "acknowledge thine iniquity" (repent), and repeatedly calls for their return (v.14-)

God invited Israel back into fellowship with Him on the basis of acknowledging her sin and changing her ways, giving no heed to the instruction that Moses gave in Deuteronomy 24:1-4, because "from the beginning it was not so."

In Jeremiah 3:8, the Lord had put her (Israel) away and given her a bill of divorcement. But in verses 1 and 12, He invites her to return and in verse 14 He offers the terms of reconciliation. In Malachi it is written, Judah hath dealt treacherously, and an abomination is committed in Israel and in Jerusalem; for Judah hath profaned the holiness of the LORD which he loved, and hath married the daughter of a strange god –Malachi 2:11.

God's divorcing of Israel and Israel's subsequent remarriage to a strange god in no way interfered with them returning to their first marriage. Instead, the Lord invited them back if they would repent, Jeremiah 3:13-14. By the time of Deuteronomy chapter 24 and through most of the Old Testament, divorce was the accepted normal, with mankind attempting to put some regulations on it, "but from the beginning it was not so."

In the book of Hosea, we have a biblical example of the reuniting of a separated or divorced first marriage: … And the LORD said to Hosea, Go, take unto thee a wife of whoredoms and children of whoredoms: for the land hath committed great whoredom, departing from the LORD –Hosea 1:2 (see also Hosea 2:5).

Sometime after Hosea marries her, she resorts to the life of a "harlot'' (Hosea 3:3) and goes after other "lovers" (2:7). When she refers to Hosea as "my first husband" (2:7), it is evidence that she likely remarried after deserting Hosea. (2:14) By Hosea patiently "alluring her and speaking comfortably to her" (2:19-20), Hosea betrothed her again and Gomer apparently responded (2:20) "in faithfulness” and came to "know the Lord." (3:3) Eventually, Hosea and Gomer both reunited with a commitment of faithfulness to each other.

Restoration to the initial God-ordained commitment is the goal, reconciliation is the process, and a repentant heart before the Lord for His mercy and forgiveness is the means (see Hosea 3:5).

John 4:1-42 is a scripture that some would interpret as objecting to the reuniting of a first marriage after a separation or divorce, because of Jesus' reply to the woman. After she said …I have no husband. Jesus said unto her, Thou hast well said, I have no husband: For thou hast had five husbands; and he whom thou now hast is not thy husband: in that saidst thou truly –John 4:17-18.

Some would interpret Jesus to be saying, "You are right woman, none of your five former husbands of which you have divorced or put away (including your first one) are your husband, and neither is the one you have now. Some commentators and others refer to this woman as a five-time divorcee and currently living with a man in an unmarried state. However, I find no evidence in this account that this woman was living an unholy life.

Jesus' purpose of this account is to reveal Himself as the "Messias" with "Living Water" to this woman and many more in Sychar. Jesus says nothing to fault or correct her, which He typically would when meeting with sin. All five husbands could have been passed away and the one she was now seeing, just a friend, perhaps anticipating marriage. Also, we don't know since it doesn't say, but she seemed to be a woman of respect and influence in the city, which would have been unlikely with an ongoing reputation of immorality. Jesus would surely have said something to inform her of her sin, when making available His Living Water. So, to use this account and say that all five husbands are adulterous and still classified as God-recorded husbands does not agree with the rest of Scripture. Nor does it support the context of the statement: he whom thou now hast is not thy husband. To claim that this story is a display of an immoral lifestyle with no known biblical evidence is close to “adding to” or “taking away” from the Scriptures. (See Revelation 22:18)

In conclusion… In our world today and in history past, mankind has attempted to equate subsequent marriages following a divorce, to the level of the initial marriage covenant. This has confused the emphasis and intent God has put on the initial marriage covenant. God's Word teaches that the Lord has always respected repentance in the restoration of any initial God-blessed covenant. For the Lord to bless and prosper the reconciling of any struggling relationship, He requires a broken, contrite spirit of humility and repentance with submission.

The context of 1 Corinthians 7:10-16 is that of a believer being in a covenant relationship with a spouse who is an unbeliever. In verse 15, the remaining believing spouse is not under obligation to denounce their walk of faith to continue a marriage relationship, neither are they free to remarry (verse 11) in the event of the unbelieving spouse leaving. If verse 15 is speaking of the marriage covenant, then verse 39 would contradict verse 15 and the will of God according to the rest of Scripture, (see Matthew 19:5 and 1 Corinthians 7:10). Living separately limits influence to the family and is a negative witness to the community, thus the believing spouse will always have a much greater impact for the Lord by staying true to the “initial marriage commitment” as challenging as that may be.

The Word of God holds the initial marriage covenant exclusively binding and honorable. Any subsequent marriage vow while either spouse is living is considered by our Lord as the sin of lust and adultery and must be repented of if we wish to seek God’s forgiveness.

Therefore, repentance and forgiveness by both spouses, with the desire to reunite and honor their initial God-blessed marriage covenant, is not a desire of the flesh but is the work of the Holy Spirit deep within the heart of the sinner. When there is a godly desire to repent and reconcile a broken relationship, we should fall on our knees in support and sincere gratitude to our Heavenly Father.

Jesus has offered to come between and restore struggling relationships that through humility and repentance seek forgiveness, thus returning to full service for their Lord resulting in eternal joy. He says: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them –Matthew 18:20. And Paul says, But if the Spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead dwell in you, he that raised up Christ from the dead shall also quicken your mortal bodies by his Spirit that dwelleth in you –Romans 8:11.

इसलिए वे अब दो नहीं, बल्कि एक देह हैं… –मत्ती 19:6।

विवाह-संबंध की स्थापना परमेश्वर ने समय के आरंभ में ही की थी। परमेश्वर ने उस पुरुष और स्त्री को, जो विवाह में प्रवेश कर रहे थे, विवाह को आशीष देने का प्रस्ताव भी दिया (उत्पत्ति 1:28), यदि वे उसकी सुंदरता और पवित्रता बनाए रखना चाहते थे। तब से, शैतान ने हर संभव तरीके से पवित्र विवाह के अस्तित्व को भ्रष्ट और नष्ट करने का प्रयास किया है। उत्पत्ति 4:19 में ही मनुष्य परमेश्वर की विवाह-योजना को भ्रष्ट करने के लिए बहुविवाह का प्रयोग कर रहे थे। लैव्यव्यवस्था अध्याय 21 और 22 में, “पहले प्रेम” को कानूनी रूप से समाप्त करने के लिए तलाक नामक एक व्यवस्था लागू की गई। इसमें पुनर्विवाह का विकल्प भी शामिल था। जब इसे पहली बार एक प्रथा के रूप में अपनाया गया, तो तलाक की पहल परमेश्वर ने नहीं, बल्कि मनुष्य ने की थी, और इसका उद्देश्य उस प्रतिबद्धता को समाप्त करना था जिसे तब तक जीवनभर निभाया जाने वाला माना जाता था।

इस लेख में हम कई बातों पर विचार करना चाहते हैं:

  • बाइबल विवाह के बारे में क्या सिखाती है? क्या पहले विवाह को परमेश्वर के सामने कोई विशेष स्थान प्राप्त है?
  • बाइबल तलाक के बारे में क्या सिखाती है? क्या परमेश्वर तलाक को मूल विवाह-वचन का अंत मानता है, जबकि दोनों में से कोई एक जीवन-साथी जीवित हो?
  • बाइबल अलग हुए या तलाकशुदा पहले विवाह के फिर से जुड़ने के बारे में क्या सिखाती है?

इस अध्ययन का उद्देश्य व्यापक होना है, साथ ही शास्त्रों को स्वयं अपना अर्थ समझाने देना है, ताकि टीका-टिप्पणी न्यूनतम रहे। इस लेखन का उद्देश्य परमेश्वर के वचन के अध्ययन के द्वारा उसकी इच्छा खोजने में प्रार्थनापूर्वक परिश्रम करने के लिए प्रोत्साहित करना है। लेखक ने प्रार्थनापूर्वक सभी संबंधित शास्त्रवचनों और उस संदर्भ पर विचार करने की इच्छा रखी है जिसमें वे लिखे गए थे।

परमेश्वर के दृष्टिकोण में पहले विवाह के बारे में बाइबल क्या सिखाती है?

पुराने नियम में कम-से-कम पाँच बार, प्रभु पहले विवाह का वर्णन अनन्य और जीवनभर रहने वाले संबंध के रूप में करते हैं। नए नियम में यीशु और प्रेरितों ने भी इसी दृष्टिकोण का समर्थन किया।

  1. तेरा सोता धन्य हो; और अपनी जवानी की पत्नी के साथ आनंदित रह –नीतिवचन 5:18। ध्यान दें कि अपनी जवानी की पत्नी को कितना महत्व दिया गया है।

  2. क्योंकि यहोवा ने तुझे बुलाया है—त्यागी हुई और मन में उदास स्त्री, और जवानी की पत्नी को, जब तू ठुकराई गई थी, तेरा परमेश्वर कहता है –यशायाह 54:6। अपनी जवानी की पत्नी होना और फिर बाद में ठुकराया जाना, इस त्यागी हुई स्त्री के दुख को और गहरा कर देता था।

  3. तुम पूछते हो, “क्यों?” क्योंकि यहोवा तेरे और तेरी जवानी की पत्नी के बीच साक्षी है, जिसके साथ तूने विश्वासघात किया है; फिर भी वह तेरी संगिनी और तेरी वाचा की पत्नी है। क्या उसी ने उन्हें एक नहीं बनाया? फिर भी उसमें आत्मा का अवशेष था। और उसने एक ही क्यों बनाया? ताकि वह परमेश्वर के भक्त वंश की खोज करे। इसलिए अपनी आत्मा के विषय में सावधान रहो, और कोई अपनी जवानी की पत्नी से विश्वासघात न करे। क्योंकि इस्राएल का परमेश्वर यहोवा कहता है कि वह त्यागने से घृणा करता है; सेनाओं का यहोवा कहता है, क्योंकि मनुष्य अपने वस्त्र से हिंसा को ढाँपता है। इसलिए अपनी आत्मा के विषय में सावधान रहो, और विश्वासघात न करो। –मलाकी 2:14-16। और वे एक-दूसरे के लिए अनन्य होकर एक क्यों बनाए गए? ताकि प्रभु के लिए भक्त वंश उत्पन्न करें। यद्यपि परमेश्वर त्यागने से घृणा करता है, फिर भी मनुष्य इसे “तलाक” नामक नागरिक और कानूनी स्वीकृति के वस्त्र से ढाँपने का प्रयास करते हैं।

  4. मत्ती 19:3-12: पद 4, “आरंभ में…” जब फरीसियों ने इस विषय पर यीशु से पूछा, तो वह उन्हें फटकारते हुए अपने पिता की मूल मंशा की ओर वापस ले जाते हैं… उसने उत्तर दिया, “क्या तुमने नहीं पढ़ा कि जिसने उन्हें आरंभ में बनाया, उसने उन्हें नर और नारी बनाया” –मत्ती 19:4। फिर वह उन्हें शास्त्रों की इस शिक्षा की याद दिलाते हैं कि “…पुरुष अपने माता-पिता को छोड़कर अपनी पत्नी से मिला रहेगा, और वे दोनों एक तन होंगे? इसलिए वे अब दो नहीं, बल्कि एक तन हैं। इसलिये जिसे परमेश्वर ने जोड़ा है, उसे मनुष्य अलग न करे” –मत्ती 19:5-6। विवाह, तलाक और पुनर्विवाह के तथ्यों का निर्णय करते समय मनुष्य के अधिकार (नागरिक न्यायालय) को परमेश्वर के अधिकार के बराबर न मानें। हमें याद रखना चाहिए कि स्वर्ग में प्रत्येक विवाह को परमेश्वर ने जोड़ा है और जीवन की पुस्तक में दर्ज किया है।

  5. जिस स्त्री का पति है, वह व्यवस्था के अनुसार अपने पति के जीते-जी उससे बँधी रहती है; परन्तु यदि पति मर जाए, तो वह पति की व्यवस्था से छूट जाती है। इसलिए यदि पति के जीते-जी वह किसी दूसरे पुरुष की हो जाए, तो व्यभिचारिणी कहलाएगी; परन्तु यदि पति मर जाए, तो वह उस व्यवस्था से स्वतंत्र है, और किसी दूसरे पुरुष की हो जाने पर भी व्यभिचारिणी नहीं होती –रोमियों 7:2-3। फिर से, सत्य का आधार स्थापित करने के लिए यह आरंभ की ओर संकेत करता है।

स्वर्गीय अभिलेखों में प्रारंभिक विवाह-वाचा को केवल किसी एक जीवन-साथी की मृत्यु ही समाप्त करेगी। और जब यह जीवन समाप्त हो जाएगा, तब अनंतकाल तक केवल स्वर्गीय अभिलेख ही महत्व रखेंगे।

बाइबल के आदर्श के कुछ अपवाद हैं:

  • एक दूसरे को वंचित न करो [बंचित रखो, रोककर रखो], केवल कुछ समय के लिए आपसी सहमति से, ताकि तुम उपवास और प्रार्थना में लगे रह सको; और फिर मिलो, ऐसा न हो कि आत्मसंयम की कमी [आत्मसंयम का अभाव] के कारण शैतान तुम्हारी परीक्षा ले –1 कुरिन्थियों 7:5। अतः, जब किसी अत्यंत महत्वपूर्ण विषय पर परमेश्वर की कृपा या मार्गदर्शन पाने की आवश्यकता हो, तो पति और पत्नी दोनों की स्वेच्छापूर्ण सहमति से कुछ समय के लिए वैवाहिक संबंध से विरत रहने पर कुछ परिस्थितियों में परमेश्वर की आशीष मिल सकती है। लेकिन इसमें तभी शामिल होना चाहिए जब दोनों जीवन-साथियों को यह स्पष्ट समझ और प्रतिबद्धता हो कि वे कब और कैसे फिर साथ आएँगे, कहीं ऐसा न हो कि शैतान तुम्हारी परीक्षा ले। इस अपवाद की तीन स्पष्ट शर्तें हैं… 1) आपसी सहमति से, 2) कुछ समय के लिए, और 3) अपने आप को प्रार्थना और उपवास में लगाने के उद्देश्य से।

  • विवाहितों को मैं आज्ञा देता हूँ—मैं नहीं, परन्तु प्रभु—कि पत्नी अपने पति से अलग न हो; और यदि अलग हो जाए, तो अविवाहित रहे, या अपने पति से मेल कर ले; और पति भी अपनी पत्नी को न छोड़े –1 कुरिन्थियों 7:10-11। यह शास्त्र का वह अंश है जो निर्दोष जीवन-साथी को बाइबिल के अनुसार दोष से मुक्त करता है, जब अलग होने का निर्णय दूसरे जीवन-साथी ने लिया हो। फिर भी यह शिक्षा बनी रहती है कि वे किसी दूसरे से विवाह न करें, “जब तक मूल जीवन-साथी जीवित है।”

तलाक के बारे में परमेश्वर के दृष्टिकोण पर बाइबल क्या सिखाती है?

“कहा गया है, जो कोई अपनी पत्नी को त्यागे, वह उसे तलाकनामा दे। परन्तु मैं तुम से कहता हूँ, जो कोई व्यभिचार के कारण को छोड़ किसी और कारण से अपनी पत्नी को त्यागता है, वह उससे व्यभिचार कराता है; और जो कोई त्यागी हुई स्त्री से विवाह करता है, वह व्यभिचार करता है” –मत्ती 5:31-32। अपने पहाड़ी उपदेश में लोगों को सिखाते समय यीशु जिन अनेक बातों पर बार-बार ध्यान केंद्रित करते रहे, उनमें से एक विवाह के लिए परमेश्वर की मूल योजना का यह विषय था।

“व्यभिचार के कारण को छोड़कर” विवाह से पहले की किसी भी प्रकार की अनैतिकता को व्यभिचार कहा गया है। आधुनिक ईसाई धर्म में कभी-कभी इस विचार को समझने में कठिनाई होती है, क्योंकि प्राचीन यहूदी संस्कृति की प्रथाएँ बहुत पहले भुला दी गई हैं। यहूदी संस्कृति में मंगनी की अवधि को विवाह-समारोह जितना ही बाध्यकारी माना जाता था; यहाँ तक कि मंगनी समाप्त करने के लिए “तलाक” आवश्यक था। इस आधारभूत समझ के अनुसार, यहाँ व्यभिचार का आशय मंगनी या विवाह-पूर्व वचनबद्धता की अवधि के दौरान की अनैतिकता से है। यदि कोई बेवफाई सामने आती, तो मंगनी या विवाह-पूर्व वचनबद्धता को तोड़ने के लिए तलाकनामा आवश्यक था। तलाक के इस विशेष पहलू की यीशु ने आलोचना नहीं की। मंगनी की अवधि में उन्हें वैवाहिक शारीरिक संबंध रखने की अनुमति नहीं थी, फिर भी उन्हें पति-पत्नी कहा जाता था। अंततः, इसे व्यभिचार के बजाय अनैतिक यौन संबंध इसलिए कहा गया है कि मंगनी की अवधि में दोनों का विवाह अभी हुआ नहीं होता, न ही उनका शारीरिक संबंध स्थापित हुआ होता। इसलिए, परमेश्वर की दृष्टि में उनके विवाहित माने जाने के समय से ठीक पहले, किसी बाहरी संबंध को व्यभिचार कहा जाएगा; जबकि उनके विवाहित माने जाने के ठीक बाद, ऐसा ही कोई संबंध जारकर्म होगा।

आगे दिए गए पदों में इस स्थिति का एक उत्कृष्ट बाइबिल उदाहरण यूसुफ और मरियम के साथ मिलता है: यीशु मसीह का जन्म इस प्रकार हुआ: जब उसकी माता मरियम की मंगनी यूसुफ से हुई थी, और उनके एक साथ आने से पहले, वह पवित्र आत्मा की ओर से गर्भवती पाई गई। तब उसका पति यूसुफ, जो धर्मी था और उसे लोगों के सामने लज्जित नहीं करना चाहता था, उसे चुपचाप त्याग देने की सोचने लगा –मत्ती 1:18, 19।

इसलिए, बाइबिल की दृष्टि से तलाक नागरिक कानून के अनुसार पहले विवाह को तोड़ सकता है, परन्तु परमेश्वर के सामने पहले विवाह को समाप्त नहीं कर सकता। तलाकशुदा व्यक्ति अपने पहले विवाह का साथी बना रहता है (जब तक दूसरा जीवन-साथी जीवित है), यहाँ तक कि पुनर्विवाह करने पर भी, चाहे उनका कानूनी तलाक हुआ हो या नहीं; इस प्रकार दोनों पक्ष बाइबिल के अनुसार व्यभिचार में पड़ते हैं। लेकिन जब तलाक को प्रारंभिक विवाह-वाचा को तोड़ने या रद्द करने में वैध माना जाता है, तो इस प्रकार हम वह विशेष कारण ही हटा देते हैं जिसके आधार पर परमेश्वर बाद के विवाहों को व्यभिचार कहता है।

मत्ती 19:3-10 में यीशु वही शिक्षा दे रहे हैं जो मत्ती 5:31-32 में है। लेकिन मत्ती 19:3-10 की शुरुआत फरीसियों के यीशु को एक प्रश्न से फँसाने के प्रयास से हुई: उन्होंने उससे कहा, “तो फिर मूसा ने क्यों आज्ञा दी कि तलाकनामा देकर उसे त्याग दो?” –मत्ती 19:7। तब यीशु आगे उत्तर देते हैं और कहते हैं, “…मूसा ने तुम्हारे मन की कठोरता के कारण तुम्हें अपनी पत्नियों को त्यागने की अनुमति दी; परन्तु आरंभ से ऐसा नहीं था” –मत्ती 19:8।

मरकुस में भी लिखा है, “परन्तु सृष्टि के आरंभ से परमेश्वर ने उन्हें नर और नारी बनाया। इस कारण पुरुष अपने माता-पिता को छोड़कर अपनी पत्नी से मिला रहेगा; और वे दोनों एक तन होंगे। इसलिए वे अब दो नहीं, बल्कि एक तन हैं। इसलिये जिसे परमेश्वर ने जोड़ा है, उसे मनुष्य अलग न करे” –मरकुस 10:6-9।

इस प्रकार, तलाक और उससे जुड़े सभी नियम, नागरिक कानून का उपयोग करके उस संबंध को समाप्त करने का मनुष्य का प्रयास हैं जिसे आरंभ से ही किसी एक जीवन-साथी की मृत्यु तक का माना गया था।

अलग हुए या तलाकशुदा पहले विवाह के फिर से जुड़ने के बारे में बाइबल क्या सिखाती है?

उसने उनसे कहा, “मूसा ने तुम्हारे मन की कठोरता के कारण तुम्हें अपनी पत्नियों को त्यागने की अनुमति दी; परन्तु आरंभ से ऐसा नहीं था” –मत्ती 19:8। यहाँ यीशु अपने पिता की मूल मंशा सिखा रहे हैं। व्यवस्था में मूसा ने सिखाया कि… “जब कोई पुरुष किसी स्त्री को ब्याहकर अपनी पत्नी बना ले, और ऐसा हो कि वह उसकी दृष्टि में अनुग्रह न पाए, क्योंकि उसने उसमें कुछ अशुद्धता पाई है, तो वह उसके लिए तलाकनामा लिखकर उसके हाथ में दे, और उसे अपने घर से निकाल दे। और जब वह उसके घर से निकल जाए, तो वह दूसरे पुरुष की पत्नी हो सकती है। और यदि दूसरा पति उससे बैर रखे, और उसके लिए तलाकनामा लिखकर उसके हाथ में दे, और उसे अपने घर से निकाल दे; या यदि वह दूसरा पति, जिसने उसे अपनी पत्नी बनाया था, मर जाए; तो उसका पहला पति, जिसने उसे त्याग दिया था, उसे फिर अपनी पत्नी नहीं बना सकता… –व्यवस्थाविवरण 24:1-4।

तलाक की अनुमति और उसकी शर्तों के विषय में मूसा की यही शिक्षा थी, जिसके बारे में यीशु ने समझाया कि यह उनके मन की कठोरता के कारण थी। यीशु ने आगे यह कहकर इसे और स्पष्ट किया, परन्तु आरंभ से ऐसा नहीं था –मत्ती 19:8।

शायद यिर्मयाह भी व्यवस्थाविवरण 24:1-4 में मूसा के लेख की ओर संकेत कर रहे हैं, जब वे कहते हैं, “वे कहते हैं, यदि कोई पुरुष अपनी पत्नी को त्याग दे, और वह उससे दूर होकर किसी दूसरे पुरुष की हो जाए, तो क्या वह फिर उसके पास लौट सकता है? क्या वह देश अत्यन्त अशुद्ध न हो जाएगा? परन्तु तूने अनेक प्रेमियों के साथ व्यभिचार किया है; फिर भी मेरे पास लौट आ, यहोवा की यही वाणी है” –यिर्मयाह 3:1। यिर्मयाह अध्याय 3 का शेष भाग कहता है कि यदि वे पश्चात्ताप करें तो परमेश्वर उन्हें वापस ग्रहण करता है। परमेश्वर उनसे आग्रह करता है कि वे (पद 13) “अपने अधर्म को मान लें” (पश्चात्ताप करें), और बार-बार उन्हें लौटने के लिए बुलाता है (पद 14-)।

परमेश्वर ने इस्राएल को उसके साथ फिर से संगति में आने का निमंत्रण उसके पाप को स्वीकार करने और अपनी चाल बदलने के आधार पर दिया; उसने व्यवस्थाविवरण 24:1-4 में मूसा के निर्देश पर ध्यान नहीं दिया, क्योंकि “आरंभ से ऐसा नहीं था।”

यिर्मयाह 3:8 में प्रभु ने उसे (इस्राएल को) त्याग दिया था और तलाकनामा दे दिया था। लेकिन पद 1 और 12 में वह उसे लौटने का निमंत्रण देता है, और पद 14 में मेल-मिलाप की शर्तें प्रस्तुत करता है। मलाकी में लिखा है, “यहूदा ने विश्वासघात किया है, और इस्राएल और यरूशलेम में घृणित काम हुआ है; क्योंकि यहूदा ने यहोवा के उस पवित्रस्थान को अपवित्र किया है जिससे वह प्रेम करता था, और पराए देवता की बेटी से विवाह किया है” –मलाकी 2:11।

इस्राएल को परमेश्वर द्वारा त्यागे जाने और इस्राएल के बाद में पराए देवता से विवाह करने से किसी भी तरह उनके अपने पहले विवाह में लौटने में बाधा नहीं आई। इसके बजाय, यदि वे पश्चात्ताप करते तो प्रभु ने उन्हें लौटने का निमंत्रण दिया, यिर्मयाह 3:13-14। व्यवस्थाविवरण अध्याय 24 के समय तक और पुराने नियम के अधिकांश भाग में, तलाक सामान्य और स्वीकृत प्रथा बन गया था, और मनुष्य उस पर कुछ नियम लगाने का प्रयास कर रहे थे; “परन्तु आरंभ से ऐसा नहीं था।”

होशे की पुस्तक में, अलग हुए या तलाकशुदा पहले विवाह के फिर से जुड़ने का बाइबिल उदाहरण मिलता है: … और यहोवा ने होशे से कहा, “जा, वेश्यागमन करने वाली स्त्री और वेश्यागमन से उत्पन्न बच्चों को अपने पास ले; क्योंकि देश ने यहोवा को छोड़कर बड़ा व्यभिचार किया है” –होशे 1:2 (होशे 2:5 भी देखें)।

होशे के उससे विवाह करने के कुछ समय बाद, वह “वेश्या” का जीवन अपनाती है (होशे 3:3) और दूसरे “प्रेमियों” के पीछे जाती है (2:7)। जब वह होशे को “मेरा पहला पति” (2:7) कहती है, तो यह इस बात का प्रमाण है कि होशे को छोड़ने के बाद शायद उसने पुनर्विवाह कर लिया था। (2:14) होशे धैर्यपूर्वक “उसे लुभाकर और उससे मधुर बातें करके” (2:19-20), उससे फिर मंगनी करता है और गोमेर ने स्पष्टतः (2:20) “विश्वासयोग्यता में” उत्तर दिया और “यहोवा को जानने” लगी। (3:3) अंततः, होशे और गोमेर एक-दूसरे के प्रति विश्वासयोग्य रहने की प्रतिबद्धता के साथ फिर से एक हो गए।

परमेश्वर द्वारा ठहराई गई मूल प्रतिबद्धता की बहाली लक्ष्य है, मेल-मिलाप प्रक्रिया है, और प्रभु के सामने पश्चात्तापी हृदय के साथ उसकी दया और क्षमा माँगना साधन है (होशे 3:5 देखें)।

यूहन्ना 4:1-42 ऐसा शास्त्रवचन है जिसे कुछ लोग अलगाव या तलाक के बाद पहले विवाह के फिर से जुड़ने पर आपत्ति के रूप में समझेंगे, क्योंकि यीशु ने उस स्त्री को उत्तर दिया था। जब उसने कहा, “…मेरा कोई पति नहीं है।” यीशु ने उससे कहा, “तूने ठीक कहा, ‘मेरा कोई पति नहीं है,’ क्योंकि तेरे पाँच पति हो चुके हैं; और जिसे तू अब रखती है, वह तेरा पति नहीं है; यह तूने सच कहा” –यूहन्ना 4:17-18।

कुछ लोग यीशु की बात का अर्थ यह समझेंगे: “तू सही कहती है, स्त्री, जिन पाँच पूर्व पतियों से तूने तलाक लिया या जिन्हें त्यागा (जिसमें तेरा पहला पति भी शामिल है), उनमें से कोई तेरा पति नहीं है, और जिसे तू अभी रखती है, वह भी नहीं।” कुछ टीकाकार और अन्य लोग इस स्त्री को पाँच बार तलाकशुदा और वर्तमान में एक पुरुष के साथ अविवाहित अवस्था में रहने वाली बताते हैं। हालाँकि, मुझे इस विवरण में ऐसा कोई प्रमाण नहीं मिलता कि यह स्त्री अपवित्र जीवन जी रही थी।

इस विवरण में यीशु का उद्देश्य इस स्त्री और सिखार के कई अन्य लोगों के सामने स्वयं को “मसीहा” और “जीवन का जल” के रूप में प्रकट करना है। यीशु उसे दोष देने या सुधारने के लिए कुछ नहीं कहते, जबकि पाप के साथ सामना होने पर वह सामान्यतः ऐसा करते। संभव है कि पाँचों पति मर चुके हों, और जिस पुरुष से वह अब मिल रही थी, वह केवल एक मित्र हो, शायद विवाह की आशा रखते हुए। हम यह भी नहीं जानते, क्योंकि विवरण ऐसा नहीं कहता; लेकिन वह नगर में सम्मानित और प्रभावशाली स्त्री जान पड़ती थी, जो अनैतिकता की निरंतर प्रतिष्ठा होने पर संभवतः न होता। अपना जीवन का जल देते समय यीशु निश्चित ही उसे उसके पाप के बारे में बताने के लिए कुछ कहते। इसलिए, इस विवरण का उपयोग करके यह कहना कि पाँचों पति व्यभिचारी हैं और परमेश्वर के अभिलेखों में अब भी पति के रूप में दर्ज हैं, शेष शास्त्रों से मेल नहीं खाता। न ही यह इस कथन के संदर्भ का समर्थन करता है: “जिसे तू अब रखती है, वह तेरा पति नहीं है।” किसी ज्ञात बाइबिल प्रमाण के बिना इस कहानी को अनैतिक जीवनशैली का चित्रण बताना, शास्त्रों में “बढ़ाने” या “घटाने” के निकट है। (प्रकाशितवाक्य 22:18 देखें)

Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh… –Matthew 19:6.

The marriage relationship was authored by God in the very beginning of time. God also offered to bless the marriage (Genesis 1:28) of the man and woman entering into it, if they desired to maintain its beauty and holiness. Since then, Satan has attempted, in every way possible, to corrupt and destroy the existence of Holy Matrimony. As early as Genesis 4:19, mankind was using polygamy to corrupt God's design of marriage. In Leviticus chapters 21 and 22, a plan, called a divorce, was put in place to legally dissolve the “first love”. This also included the option to remarry. When it was first developed as a practice, the call for divorce was initiated by man, not God, and was for the purpose of dissolving what was understood up until that time to be a lifelong commitment.

In this article we want to look at a number of points:

  • What does the Bible teach about marriage? Does the first marriage carry any special position with God?
  • What does the Bible teach about divorce? Does God recognize divorce as terminating the original marriage vow while either spouse is still living?
  • What does the Bible teach about the reuniting of a separated or divorced first marriage?

It is the desire of this study to be comprehensive, while allowing the scriptures to be their own interpreter, thus keeping commentary to a minimum. The purpose of this writing is to encourage diligence with prayer in seeking the will of God through a study of His Word. The desire of the writer has been to prayerfully consider all relevant scriptures and the context for which they were written.

What does the Bible teach about God's view of the first marriage?

At least five times in the Old Testament, the first marriage is described by the Lord as exclusive and lifelong. This same view was supported by Jesus and the apostles in the New Testament.

  1. Let thy fountain be blessed: and rejoice with the wife of thy youth –Proverbs 5:18. Note the attention given to the wife of thy youth.

  2. For the LORD hath called thee as a woman forsaken and grieved in spirit, and a wife of youth, when thou wast refused, saith thy God –Isaiah 54:6. Being a wife of one’s youth and then later refused, intensified the grieving of this forsaken woman.

  3. Yet ye say, Wherefore? Because the LORD hath been witness between thee and the wife of thy youth, against whom thou hast dealt treacherously: yet is she thy companion, and the wife of thy covenant. And did not he make one? Yet had he the residue of the spirit. And wherefore one? That he might seek a godly seed. Therefore take heed to your spirit, and let none deal treacherously against the wife of his youth. For the LORD, the God of Israel, saith that he hateth putting away: for one covereth violence with his garment, saith the LORD of hosts: therefore take heed to your spirit, that ye deal not treacherously. –Malachi 2:14-16. And why are they made one, exclusive to each other? To raise up a godly seed unto the Lord. Even though God hates putting away, men still try to cover it with a garment of civil, legal acceptance called "divorce".

  4. Matthew 19:3-12: V.4 In the beginning… Jesus, when asked by the Pharisees about this issue, takes them back to original intent of His Father when He chides them… And he answered and said unto them, Have ye not read, that he which made them at the beginning made them male and female –Matthew 19:4. He then goes on to remind them of the Scriptures teaching that …a man [shall] leave [his] father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they twain shall be one flesh? Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder –Matthew 19:5-6. Don't equate man’s authority (the civil court) with God’s authority when it comes to deciding what the facts are concerning marriage, divorce, and remarriage. We need to remember that it is God who has joined each marriage together in Heaven and has recorded them in the Book of Life.

  5. For the woman which hath an husband is bound by the law to her husband so long as he liveth; but if the husband be dead, she is loosed from the law of her husband. So then if, while her husband liveth, she be married to another man, she shall be called an adulteress: but if her husband be dead, she is free from that law; so that she is no adulteress, though she be married to another man –Romans 7:2-3. Again, this is pointing back to the beginning in order to establish a basis of Truth.

Only the death of either spouse will terminate the initial marriage covenant in the heavenly records. And once this life is over, only the heavenly records will matter—for all of eternity.

There are several exceptions to the Biblical ideal:

  • Defraud [deprive, keep back] ye not one the other, except it be with consent for a time, that ye may give yourselves to fasting and prayer; and come together again, that Satan tempt you not for your incontinency [lack of self-restraint] –1 Corinthians 7:5. So, restraining the marriage relationship for a time with voluntary consent from both husband and wife when there is a need for seeking God’s favor or guidance on a matter of great importance, may in some circumstances find God’s blessing. However, this should only be engaged in with a clear understanding and commitment by both spouses involved, about when and how to come together again, lest Satan tempt you. This exception has three clear qualifiers… 1) with consent, 2) for a time, & 3) for the purpose of giving yourselves to prayer and fasting.

  • And unto the married I command, yet not I, but the Lord, Let not the wife depart from her husband: But and if she depart, let her remain unmarried, or be reconciled to her husband: and let not the husband put away his wife –1 Corinthians 7:10-11. This is the Scriptural passage that frees the innocent spouse from biblical guilt when the other spouse is the one who chose to part ways. However, the teaching still remains that they shall not marry another “so long as the original partner remains alive”.

What does the Bible teach about God's view of divorce?

It hath been said, Whosoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorcement: But I say unto you, That whosoever shall put away his wife, saving for the cause of fornication, causeth her to commit adultery: and whosoever shall marry her that is divorced committeth adultery –Matthew 5:31-32. As Jesus taught the people in His Sermon on the Mount, one of the many things that He kept focusing on was this issue of God’s original plan for marriage.

“Saving for the cause of fornication” Fornication is any type of immorality prior to marriage. Modern-day Christianity, at times, struggles with this idea since the customs of the ancient Jewish culture have long since been forgotten. In Jewish culture, the betrothal period was considered almost as binding as the marriage ceremony itself, so much so that to end a betrothal required a “divorce”. With this as a foundational understanding, fornication here is speaking of immorality during the espousal or betrothal period. If any unfaithfulness was discovered, a writing of divorcement was required to break the betrothal, espousal, or engagement. This specific aspect of divorce was not criticized by Jesus. Even though they were not permitted to engage in the physical relationship of marriage during the betrothal period, they were still referred to as husband and wife. Finally, the reason this is referred to as fornication instead of adultery is because that during the betrothal period the marriage of the two has not yet taken place, nor has their relationship been consummated physically. Thus, just prior to the point in time when they are considered by God as being married, any outside relationship would be fornication, while just after they are considered married, any similar relationship would be adultery.

We have an excellent biblical example of this type of situation with Joseph & Mary in the following verses: Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost. Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily –Matthew 1:18, 19.

So, biblically speaking, divorce can put asunder the first marriage according to civil law but cannot terminate a first marriage before God. A divorced person remains the companion of their first marriage (as long as the other spouse is alive) even when remarrying, whether they are legally divorced or not, thus resulting in biblical adultery for both parties. However, when divorce is allowed to be recognized as being legitimate in breaking or annulling the initial marriage covenant, we have thereby removed the specific reason by which God calls subsequent marriages adultery.

In Matthew 19:3-10, Jesus is teaching the same lesson as in Matthew 5:31-32. However, Matthew 19:3-10 was initiated from an attempt by the Pharisees to trap Jesus with a question: They say unto him, Why did Moses then command to give a writing of divorcement, and to put her away? –Matthew 19:7. Jesus then responds further and says, …Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so –Matthew 19:8.

Also, in Mark it is written, But from the beginning of the creation God made them male and female. For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and cleave to his wife; And they twain shall be one flesh: so then they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder –Mark 10:6-9.

Thus, divorce, with all its regulations, is man's attempt to use civil law to terminate that which from the beginning was understood to be until the death of either spouse.

What does the Bible teach about the reuniting of a separated or a divorced first marriage?

He saith unto them, Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so –Matthew 19:8. Here Jesus is teaching the initial mind of His Father. In the law, Moses taught that… When a man hath taken a wife, and married her, and it come to pass that she find no favour in his eyes, because he hath found some uncleanness in her: then let him write her a bill of divorcement, and give it in her hand, and send her out of his house. And when she is departed out of his house, she may go and be another man's wife. And if the latter husband hate her, and write her a bill of divorcement, and giveth it in her hand, and sendeth her out of his house; or if the latter husband die, which took her to be his wife; Her former husband, which sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife… –Deuteronomy 24:1-4.

This is Moses' teaching regarding permission and qualifications for divorce which Jesus explained was because of the hardness of their hearts. Jesus further clarified this by saying, but from the beginning it was not so –Matthew 19:8.

Perhaps Jeremiah also is referring to Moses' writing in Deuteronomy 24:1-4 when he says, They say, If a man put away his wife, and she go from him, and become another man's, shall he return unto her again? shall not that land be greatly polluted? but thou hast played the harlot with many lovers; yet return again to me, saith the LORD –Jeremiah 3:1. The remainder of Jeremiah chapter 3 speaks of God receiving them back if they repent. God pleads for them to (v.13) "acknowledge thine iniquity" (repent), and repeatedly calls for their return (v.14-)

God invited Israel back into fellowship with Him on the basis of acknowledging her sin and changing her ways, giving no heed to the instruction that Moses gave in Deuteronomy 24:1-4, because "from the beginning it was not so."

In Jeremiah 3:8, the Lord had put her (Israel) away and given her a bill of divorcement. But in verses 1 and 12, He invites her to return and in verse 14 He offers the terms of reconciliation. In Malachi it is written, Judah hath dealt treacherously, and an abomination is committed in Israel and in Jerusalem; for Judah hath profaned the holiness of the LORD which he loved, and hath married the daughter of a strange god –Malachi 2:11.

God's divorcing of Israel and Israel's subsequent remarriage to a strange god in no way interfered with them returning to their first marriage. Instead, the Lord invited them back if they would repent, Jeremiah 3:13-14. By the time of Deuteronomy chapter 24 and through most of the Old Testament, divorce was the accepted normal, with mankind attempting to put some regulations on it, "but from the beginning it was not so."

In the book of Hosea, we have a biblical example of the reuniting of a separated or divorced first marriage: … And the LORD said to Hosea, Go, take unto thee a wife of whoredoms and children of whoredoms: for the land hath committed great whoredom, departing from the LORD –Hosea 1:2 (see also Hosea 2:5).

Sometime after Hosea marries her, she resorts to the life of a "harlot'' (Hosea 3:3) and goes after other "lovers" (2:7). When she refers to Hosea as "my first husband" (2:7), it is evidence that she likely remarried after deserting Hosea. (2:14) By Hosea patiently "alluring her and speaking comfortably to her" (2:19-20), Hosea betrothed her again and Gomer apparently responded (2:20) "in faithfulness” and came to "know the Lord." (3:3) Eventually, Hosea and Gomer both reunited with a commitment of faithfulness to each other.

Restoration to the initial God-ordained commitment is the goal, reconciliation is the process, and a repentant heart before the Lord for His mercy and forgiveness is the means (see Hosea 3:5).

John 4:1-42 is a scripture that some would interpret as objecting to the reuniting of a first marriage after a separation or divorce, because of Jesus' reply to the woman. After she said …I have no husband. Jesus said unto her, Thou hast well said, I have no husband: For thou hast had five husbands; and he whom thou now hast is not thy husband: in that saidst thou truly –John 4:17-18.

Some would interpret Jesus to be saying, "You are right woman, none of your five former husbands of which you have divorced or put away (including your first one) are your husband, and neither is the one you have now. Some commentators and others refer to this woman as a five-time divorcee and currently living with a man in an unmarried state. However, I find no evidence in this account that this woman was living an unholy life.

Jesus' purpose of this account is to reveal Himself as the "Messias" with "Living Water" to this woman and many more in Sychar. Jesus says nothing to fault or correct her, which He typically would when meeting with sin. All five husbands could have been passed away and the one she was now seeing, just a friend, perhaps anticipating marriage. Also, we don't know since it doesn't say, but she seemed to be a woman of respect and influence in the city, which would have been unlikely with an ongoing reputation of immorality. Jesus would surely have said something to inform her of her sin, when making available His Living Water. So, to use this account and say that all five husbands are adulterous and still classified as God-recorded husbands does not agree with the rest of Scripture. Nor does it support the context of the statement: he whom thou now hast is not thy husband. To claim that this story is a display of an immoral lifestyle with no known biblical evidence is close to “adding to” or “taking away” from the Scriptures. (See Revelation 22:18)

In conclusion… In our world today and in history past, mankind has attempted to equate subsequent marriages following a divorce, to the level of the initial marriage covenant. This has confused the emphasis and intent God has put on the initial marriage covenant. God's Word teaches that the Lord has always respected repentance in the restoration of any initial God-blessed covenant. For the Lord to bless and prosper the reconciling of any struggling relationship, He requires a broken, contrite spirit of humility and repentance with submission.

The context of 1 Corinthians 7:10-16 is that of a believer being in a covenant relationship with a spouse who is an unbeliever. In verse 15, the remaining believing spouse is not under obligation to denounce their walk of faith to continue a marriage relationship, neither are they free to remarry (verse 11) in the event of the unbelieving spouse leaving. If verse 15 is speaking of the marriage covenant, then verse 39 would contradict verse 15 and the will of God according to the rest of Scripture, (see Matthew 19:5 and 1 Corinthians 7:10). Living separately limits influence to the family and is a negative witness to the community, thus the believing spouse will always have a much greater impact for the Lord by staying true to the “initial marriage commitment” as challenging as that may be.

The Word of God holds the initial marriage covenant exclusively binding and honorable. Any subsequent marriage vow while either spouse is living is considered by our Lord as the sin of lust and adultery and must be repented of if we wish to seek God’s forgiveness.

Therefore, repentance and forgiveness by both spouses, with the desire to reunite and honor their initial God-blessed marriage covenant, is not a desire of the flesh but is the work of the Holy Spirit deep within the heart of the sinner. When there is a godly desire to repent and reconcile a broken relationship, we should fall on our knees in support and sincere gratitude to our Heavenly Father.

Jesus has offered to come between and restore struggling relationships that through humility and repentance seek forgiveness, thus returning to full service for their Lord resulting in eternal joy. He says: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them –Matthew 18:20. And Paul says, But if the Spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead dwell in you, he that raised up Christ from the dead shall also quicken your mortal bodies by his Spirit that dwelleth in you –Romans 8:11.

Kwa hiyo, si wawili tena, bali mwili mmoja… –Mathayo 19:6.

Uhusiano wa ndoa ulianzishwa na Mungu tangu mwanzo kabisa wa wakati. Mungu pia alitoa baraka kwa ndoa (Mwanzo 1:28) ya mwanamume na mwanamke wanaoingia ndani yake, ikiwa wangetaka kudumisha uzuri na utakatifu wake. Tangu wakati huo, Shetani amejaribu kwa kila njia iwezekanavyo kupotosha na kuharibu uwepo wa Ndoa Takatifu. Tangu Mwanzo 4:19, wanadamu walikuwa wakitumia ndoa za wake wengi kupotosha mpango wa Mungu kuhusu ndoa. Katika Mambo ya Walawi sura ya 21 na 22, mpango ulioitwa talaka uliwekwa ili kuvunja kisheria “upendo wa kwanza”. Hilo lilijumuisha pia uwezekano wa kuoa au kuolewa tena. Zoezi hilo lilipoanzishwa kwa mara ya kwanza, wito wa talaka ulianzishwa na mwanadamu, si Mungu, na ulikuwa na kusudi la kuvunja kile ambacho hadi wakati huo kilieleweka kuwa ahadi ya maisha yote.

Katika makala hii tunataka kuangalia mambo kadhaa:

  • Biblia inafundisha nini kuhusu ndoa? Je, ndoa ya kwanza ina nafasi ya pekee mbele za Mungu?
  • Biblia inafundisha nini kuhusu talaka? Je, Mungu hutambua talaka kuwa inasitisha kiapo cha awali cha ndoa wakati mmoja wa wenzi bado yu hai?
  • Biblia inafundisha nini kuhusu kuungana tena kwa ndoa ya kwanza iliyotengana au kuvunjika kwa talaka?

Lengo la somo hili ni kuwa pana na kamili, huku tukiziacha Maandiko yajitafsiri yenyewe, na hivyo kupunguza maelezo ya ziada kadiri iwezekanavyo. Kusudi la maandishi haya ni kuhimiza bidii ya kutafuta kwa maombi mapenzi ya Mungu kwa kujifunza Neno lake. Mwandishi amekuwa na nia ya kuyazingatia kwa maombi Maandiko yote yanayohusika pamoja na muktadha ambao yaliandikwa.

Biblia inafundisha nini kuhusu mtazamo wa Mungu juu ya ndoa ya kwanza?

Angalau mara tano katika Agano la Kale, ndoa ya kwanza inaelezwa na Bwana kuwa ya kipekee na ya kudumu maisha yote. Yesu na mitume waliunga mkono mtazamo huohuo katika Agano Jipya.

  1. Na chemchemi yako ibarikiwe; nawe umfurahie mke wa ujana wako –Mithali 5:18. Zingatia jinsi mke wa ujana wako anavyotiliwa maanani.

  2. Kwa maana Bwana amekuita kama mwanamke aliyeachwa na mwenye huzuni rohoni, kama mke wa ujana, aliyekataliwa, asema Mungu wako –Isaya 54:6. Kuwa mke wa ujana wa mtu na baadaye kukataliwa kulizidisha huzuni ya mwanamke huyu aliyeachwa.

  3. Hata hivyo mwasema, Kwa sababu gani? Kwa sababu Bwana amekuwa shahidi kati yako na mke wa ujana wako, ambaye umemtenda kwa hila; naye ni mwenzi wako, na mke wa agano lako. Je, hakuwafanya kuwa mmoja? Hata hivyo, alikuwa na salio la roho. Na kwa nini mmoja? Ili atafute uzao wa kumcha Mungu. Basi jihadharini rohoni mwenu, wala mtu asimtendee kwa hila mke wa ujana wake. Kwa maana Bwana, Mungu wa Israeli, asema ya kuwa anachukia kuachana; kwa maana mtu hufunika jeuri kama vazi lake, asema Bwana wa majeshi; basi jihadharini rohoni mwenu, msitende kwa hila. –Malaki 2:14-16. Na kwa nini walifanywa kuwa mmoja, wa kipekee kwa kila mmoja? Ili wamlee Bwana uzao unaomcha Mungu. Ingawa Mungu huchukia kuachana, watu bado hujaribu kufunika jambo hilo kwa vazi la kukubalika kwa kiraia na kisheria liitwalo “talaka”.

  4. Mathayo 19:3-12: Mstari wa 4. “Hapo mwanzo…” Yesu, alipoulizwa na Mafarisayo kuhusu jambo hili, anawarudisha kwenye kusudi la awali la Baba yake anapowakemea… Akajibu akawaambia, Hamkusoma ya kwamba yeye aliyewaumba tangu mwanzo aliwaumba mwanamume na mwanamke –Mathayo 19:4. Kisha anaendelea kuwakumbusha mafundisho ya Maandiko kwamba …mwanamume atamwacha baba yake na mama yake, ataambatana na mkewe; na hao wawili watakuwa mwili mmoja? Hata wamekuwa si wawili tena, bali mwili mmoja. Basi alichokiunganisha Mungu, mwanadamu asikitenganishe –Mathayo 19:5-6. Msiweke mamlaka ya mwanadamu (mahakama ya kiraia) sawa na mamlaka ya Mungu mnapoamua ukweli kuhusu ndoa, talaka na kuoa au kuolewa tena. Tunahitaji kukumbuka kwamba ni Mungu aliyeunganisha kila ndoa pamoja Mbinguni na kuziandika katika Kitabu cha Uzima.

  5. Kwa maana mwanamke aliye na mume amefungwa na sheria kwa mumewe maadamu yu hai; lakini mumewe akifa, amefunguliwa kutoka katika sheria ya mumewe. Basi mumewe akiwa hai, akiolewa na mume mwingine, ataitwa mzinzi; lakini mumewe akifa, yu huru na sheria hiyo, hata akiwa ameolewa na mume mwingine, si mzinzi –Warumi 7:2-3. Tena, hili linaturudisha mwanzo ili kuweka msingi wa Kweli.

Kifo cha mmoja wa wenzi pekee ndicho kitakachositisha agano la kwanza la ndoa katika kumbukumbu za mbinguni. Na maisha haya yanapokwisha, kumbukumbu za mbinguni pekee ndizo zitakazokuwa na umuhimu—milele yote.

Kuna hali kadhaa za kipekee kuhusiana na kanuni bora ya Kibiblia:

  • Msinyoane [msimnyime, msimzuie] haki yake mwenzake, isipokuwa kwa maafikiano kwa muda, ili mpate kujitolea kwa kufunga na kuomba; kisha rudianeni tena, Shetani asije akawajaribu kwa kutokuwa na kiasi kwenu [kukosa kujizuia] –1 Wakorintho 7:5. Kwa hiyo, kusitisha kwa muda uhusiano wa ndoa kwa hiari na kwa maafikiano ya mume na mke wote, wanapohitaji kutafuta kibali au mwongozo wa Mungu kuhusu jambo muhimu sana, kunaweza katika hali fulani kupata baraka za Mungu. Hata hivyo, jambo hili linapaswa kufanywa tu ikiwa wenzi wote wanaelewa wazi na wamekubaliana kuhusu lini na jinsi watakavyorudiana, ili Shetani asiwajaribu. Isipokuwa hili lina masharti matatu yaliyo wazi… 1) kwa maafikiano, 2) kwa muda, na 3) kwa kusudi la kujitolea kwa maombi na kufunga.

  • Na wale waliooa na kuolewa nawaagiza, wala si mimi, ila Bwana, mke asiachane na mumewe; lakini ikiwa ameacha, na akae asiolewe, au apatane na mumewe; tena mume asiachane na mkewe –1 Wakorintho 7:10-11. Huu ndio mstari wa Maandiko unaomweka mwenzi asiye na hatia huru na hatia ya kibiblia wakati mwenzi mwingine ndiye aliyechagua kuachana. Hata hivyo, fundisho hili bado linasema kwamba hawapaswi kuoa au kuolewa na mwingine “maadamu mwenzi wa awali yu hai”.

Biblia inafundisha nini kuhusu mtazamo wa Mungu juu ya talaka?

Imenenwa, Mtu akimwacha mkewe, na ampe hati ya talaka; lakini mimi nawaambia, Kila mtu amwachaye mkewe, isipokuwa kwa sababu ya uasherati, amfanya kuwa mzinzi; naye mtu akimwoa yule aliyeachwa azini –Mathayo 5:31-32. Yesu alipokuwa akiwafundisha watu katika Mahubiri yake ya Mlimani, mojawapo ya mambo mengi aliyoyazingatia mara kwa mara lilikuwa suala hili la mpango wa awali wa Mungu kuhusu ndoa.

“Isipokuwa kwa sababu ya uasherati” Uasherati ni aina yoyote ya ukosefu wa maadili ya ngono kabla ya ndoa. Nyakati nyingine Ukristo wa kisasa hupambana na wazo hili kwa kuwa desturi za utamaduni wa kale wa Kiyahudi zimesahaulika kwa muda mrefu. Katika utamaduni wa Kiyahudi, kipindi cha uchumba rasmi kilionwa kuwa karibu sawa na sherehe ya ndoa yenyewe kwa uzito wake, kiasi kwamba kuvunja uchumba huo kulihitaji “talaka”. Kwa msingi huu, uasherati hapa unahusu ukosefu wa maadili ya ngono katika kipindi cha uchumba rasmi. Ikiwa ukosefu wowote wa uaminifu ungegunduliwa, hati ya talaka ilihitajika ili kuvunja uchumba huo. Yesu hakukosoa kipengele hiki maalumu cha talaka. Ingawa hawakuruhusiwa kushiriki tendo la ndoa katika kipindi cha uchumba, bado waliitwa mume na mke. Hatimaye, sababu ya jambo hili kuitwa uasherati badala ya uzinzi ni kwamba katika kipindi cha uchumba, ndoa ya hao wawili ilikuwa bado haijafungwa, wala uhusiano wao haukuwa umekamilishwa kimwili. Kwa hiyo, kabla tu ya wakati ambapo Mungu anawahesabu kuwa wameoana, uhusiano wowote na mtu mwingine ungekuwa uasherati, ilhali mara tu baada ya kuhesabiwa kuwa wameoana, uhusiano kama huo ungekuwa uzinzi.

Tuna mfano bora wa kibiblia wa hali ya aina hii katika mistari ifuatayo kuhusu Yusufu na Mariamu: Basi kuzaliwa kwake Yesu Kristo kulikuwa hivi: Mariamu mama yake alipokuwa ameposwa na Yusufu, kabla hawajakaribiana, alionekana ana mimba kwa uwezo wa Roho Mtakatifu. Naye Yusufu mumewe, kwa kuwa alikuwa mtu wa haki, asitake kumfedhehesha, aliazimu kumwacha kwa siri –Mathayo 1:18, 19.

Kwa hiyo, tukizungumza kibiblia, talaka inaweza kutenganisha ndoa ya kwanza kwa mujibu wa sheria ya kiraia, lakini haiwezi kusitisha ndoa ya kwanza mbele za Mungu. Mtu aliyetalikiwa hubaki kuwa mwenzi wa ndoa yake ya kwanza (maadamu mwenzi mwingine yu hai) hata anapooa au kuolewa tena, awe ametalikiwa kisheria au la, na hivyo pande zote mbili hutenda uzinzi kibiblia. Hata hivyo, talaka inapokubaliwa kuwa halali katika kuvunja au kubatilisha agano la kwanza la ndoa, basi tunaondoa sababu hususa inayomfanya Mungu azitaje ndoa zinazofuata kuwa uzinzi.

Katika Mathayo 19:3-10, Yesu anafundisha somo lilelile kama katika Mathayo 5:31-32. Hata hivyo, Mathayo 19:3-10 ilianza baada ya Mafarisayo kujaribu kumtega Yesu kwa swali: Wakamwambia, Mbona basi Musa aliamuru mtu kumpa hati ya talaka, na kumwacha? –Mathayo 19:7. Kisha Yesu akajibu zaidi akasema, …Musa, kwa sababu ya ugumu wa mioyo yenu, aliwaruhusu kuwaacha wake zenu; lakini tangu mwanzo haikuwa hivyo –Mathayo 19:8.

Vilevile, katika Marko imeandikwa, Lakini tangu mwanzo wa kuumbwa ulimwengu, Mungu aliwaumba mwanamume na mwanamke. Kwa sababu hiyo mwanamume atamwacha baba yake na mama yake, ataambatana na mkewe; na hao wawili watakuwa mwili mmoja; basi si wawili tena, bali mwili mmoja. Basi alichokiunganisha Mungu, mwanadamu asikitenganishe –Marko 10:6-9.

Kwa hiyo, talaka, pamoja na kanuni zake zote, ni jaribio la mwanadamu kutumia sheria ya kiraia kusitisha kile ambacho tangu mwanzo kilieleweka kuwa kingedumu hadi mmoja wa wenzi afe.

Biblia inafundisha nini kuhusu kuungana tena kwa ndoa ya kwanza iliyotengana au kuvunjika kwa talaka?

Akawaambia, Musa, kwa sababu ya ugumu wa mioyo yenu, aliwaruhusu kuwaacha wake zenu: lakini tangu mwanzo haikuwa hivyo –Mathayo 19:8. Hapa Yesu anafundisha nia ya awali ya Baba yake. Katika sheria, Musa alifundisha kwamba… Mtu akitwaa mke, akaoa naye, kisha ikawa kwamba huyo mke hakupata kibali machoni pake, kwa sababu ameona jambo lisilofaa kwake; basi na amwandikie hati ya talaka, na kumpa mkononi mwake, na kumtoa katika nyumba yake. Naye akiisha kutoka katika nyumba yake, aweza kwenda kuwa mke wa mtu mwingine. Na huyo mume wa pili akimchukia, akamwandikia hati ya talaka, na kumpa mkononi mwake, na kumtoa katika nyumba yake; au huyo mume wa pili akifa, aliyemtwaa awe mkewe; mumewe wa kwanza aliyemwacha asimwoe tena… –Kumbukumbu la Torati 24:1-4.

Haya ndiyo mafundisho ya Musa kuhusu ruhusa na masharti ya talaka, ambayo Yesu alieleza kuwa yalitolewa kwa sababu ya ugumu wa mioyo yao. Yesu alifafanua zaidi jambo hili kwa kusema, lakini tangu mwanzo haikuwa hivyo –Mathayo 19:8.

Huenda Yeremia pia anarejelea maandishi ya Musa katika Kumbukumbu la Torati 24:1-4 anaposema, Watu husema, Mtu akimwacha mkewe, naye akamwacha, akawa mke wa mtu mwingine, je, atamrudia tena? Je, nchi hiyo haitatiwa unajisi sana? Lakini wewe umefanya uzinzi na wapenzi wengi; hata hivyo, rudi kwangu tena, asema Bwana –Yeremia 3:1. Sehemu iliyobaki ya Yeremia sura ya 3 inazungumzia jinsi Mungu anavyowapokea tena wakitubu. Mungu anawasihi (mstari wa 13) “ukiri uovu wako” (tubu), na kuwaita tena na tena warudi (mstari wa 14 na kuendelea).

Mungu aliwaalika Israeli warudi katika ushirika pamoja naye kwa msingi wa kukiri dhambi zake na kubadili mwenendo wake, bila kuzingatia maagizo ambayo Musa alitoa katika Kumbukumbu la Torati 24:1-4, kwa sababu “tangu mwanzo haikuwa hivyo.”

Katika Yeremia 3:8, Bwana alikuwa amemwacha Israeli na kumpa hati ya talaka. Lakini katika mistari ya 1 na 12, anamwalika arudi, na katika mstari wa 14 anatoa masharti ya upatanisho. Katika Malaki imeandikwa, Yuda ametenda kwa hila, na chukizo limetendeka katika Israeli na Yerusalemu; kwa maana Yuda amelitia unajisi patakatifu pa Bwana alipopenda, naye amemwoa binti wa mungu mgeni –Malaki 2:11.

Talaka ya Mungu kwa Israeli na kuolewa tena kwa Israeli na mungu mgeni baadaye hakukuzuia kwa njia yoyote kurudi kwao kwenye ndoa yao ya kwanza. Badala yake, Bwana aliwaalika warudi ikiwa wangetubu, Yeremia 3:13-14. Kufikia wakati wa Kumbukumbu la Torati sura ya 24 na katika sehemu kubwa ya Agano la Kale, talaka ilikuwa jambo la kawaida lililokubaliwa, huku wanadamu wakijaribu kuiwekea kanuni fulani, “lakini tangu mwanzo haikuwa hivyo.”

Katika kitabu cha Hosea, tuna mfano wa kibiblia wa kuungana tena kwa ndoa ya kwanza iliyotengana au kuvunjika kwa talaka: … Bwana akamwambia Hosea, Nenda, umwoe mwanamke wa uzinzi na watoto wa uzinzi; kwa maana nchi hii imefanya uzinzi mwingi, kwa kumwacha Bwana –Hosea 1:2 (tazama pia Hosea 2:5).

Muda fulani baada ya Hosea kumwoa, mwanamke huyo anarudia maisha ya “kahaba” (Hosea 3:3) na kuwafuata “wapenzi” wengine (2:7). Anapomwita Hosea “mume wangu wa kwanza” (2:7), hilo ni ushahidi kwamba huenda aliolewa tena baada ya kumwacha Hosea. (2:14) Kwa Hosea “kumvuta kwa subira na kusema naye kwa upole” (2:19-20), Hosea alimposa tena na inaonekana Gomeri alijibu (2:20) “kwa uaminifu” na akaja “kumjua Bwana.” (3:3) Hatimaye, Hosea na Gomeri waliungana tena na kuahidi kuwa waaminifu kwa kila mmoja.

Kurejeshwa kwenye ahadi ya awali iliyoamriwa na Mungu ndilo lengo; upatanisho ndiyo mchakato; na moyo uliotubu mbele za Bwana ili kupata rehema na msamaha wake ndiyo njia (tazama Hosea 3:5).

Yohana 4:1-42 ni andiko ambalo baadhi ya watu wangelitafsiri kuwa linapinga kuungana tena kwa ndoa ya kwanza baada ya kutengana au talaka, kwa sababu ya jibu la Yesu kwa mwanamke huyo. Baada ya kusema …Sina mume. Yesu akamwambia, Umesema vema, Sina mume: Kwa maana umekuwa na waume watano; na huyo uliye naye sasa si mume wako; hapo umesema kweli –Yohana 4:17-18.

Baadhi ya watu wangefasiri kwamba Yesu alikuwa akisema, “Uko sahihi, mama, hakuna hata mmoja kati ya waume wako watano wa zamani ambao uliwataliki au kuwaacha (akiwemo wa kwanza) aliye mume wako, wala huyo uliyenaye sasa si mume wako.” Baadhi ya wafafanuzi na watu wengine humrejelea mwanamke huyu kuwa mtu aliyetalikiwa mara tano na ambaye wakati huo alikuwa akiishi na mwanamume bila kuoana. Hata hivyo, sioni ushahidi wowote katika simulizi hili kwamba mwanamke huyu alikuwa akiishi maisha yasiyo matakatifu.

Kusudi la Yesu katika simulizi hili ni kujifunua kwa mwanamke huyu na watu wengine wengi katika Sikari kuwa ndiye “Masihi” mwenye “Maji ya Uzima”. Yesu hasemi lolote la kumlaumu au kumrekebisha, jambo ambalo kwa kawaida angefanya alipokutana na dhambi. Huenda waume wote watano walikuwa wamekufa, na huyo aliyekuwa akikutana naye wakati huo alikuwa rafiki tu, labda wakitarajia kuoana. Pia hatujui kwa kuwa simulizi halisemi, lakini alionekana kuwa mwanamke mwenye heshima na ushawishi katika mji huo, jambo ambalo lisingekuwa rahisi kama angekuwa na sifa ya kuishi katika uasherati. Bila shaka Yesu angesema jambo la kumjulisha dhambi yake alipompa Maji yake ya Uzima. Kwa hiyo, kutumia simulizi hili na kusema kwamba waume wote watano ni wazinzi na bado wameainishwa kuwa waume waliorekodiwa na Mungu hakukubaliani na sehemu nyingine za Maandiko. Wala hakuungi mkono muktadha wa kauli hii: huyo uliye naye sasa si mume wako. Kudai kwamba simulizi hili linaonyesha maisha ya uasherati bila ushahidi wowote unaojulikana wa kibiblia ni kama “kuongeza” au “kupunguza” katika Maandiko. (Tazama Ufunuo 22:18)

Kwa kumalizia… Katika dunia ya leo na katika historia, wanadamu wamejaribu kuyalinganisha ndoa zinazofuata baada ya talaka na agano la kwanza la ndoa. Jambo hili limechanganya msisitizo na kusudi ambalo Mungu ameliweka kwenye agano la kwanza la ndoa. Neno la Mungu linafundisha kwamba Bwana amekuwa akiheshimu sikuzote toba katika kurejesha agano lolote la awali lililobarikiwa na Mungu. Ili Bwana abariki na kufanikisha upatanisho wa uhusiano wowote unaokumbwa na matatizo, anahitaji roho iliyovunjika na iliyotubu, yenye unyenyekevu na kujisalimisha.

Muktadha wa 1 Wakorintho 7:10-16 ni wa mwamini aliye katika agano la ndoa na mwenzi asiyeamini. Katika mstari wa 15, mwenzi mwamini aliyebaki halazimiki kuikana njia yake ya imani ili kuendeleza uhusiano wa ndoa; wala hayuko huru kuoa au kuolewa tena (mstari wa 11) iwapo mwenzi asiyeamini ataondoka. Ikiwa mstari wa 15 unazungumzia agano la ndoa, basi mstari wa 39 ungepingana na mstari wa 15 na mapenzi ya Mungu kulingana na sehemu nyingine za Maandiko (tazama Mathayo 19:5 na 1 Wakorintho 7:10). Kuishi mbali na mwenzi hupunguza ushawishi kwa familia na ni ushuhuda mbaya kwa jamii; kwa hiyo mwenzi mwamini atakuwa na matokeo makubwa zaidi kwa ajili ya Bwana kwa kubaki mwaminifu kwa “ahadi ya awali ya ndoa”, hata ikiwa ni jambo gumu kadiri gani.

Neno la Mungu linashikilia kwamba agano la kwanza la ndoa ni la pekee, lenye nguvu ya kuwafunga wenzi na la heshima. Kiapo chochote cha ndoa kinachofuata, wakati mmoja wa wenzi bado yu hai, huhesabiwa na Bwana wetu kuwa dhambi ya tamaa na uzinzi, na ni lazima mtu atubu jambo hilo ikiwa anataka kutafuta msamaha wa Mungu.

Kwa hiyo, toba na msamaha wa wenzi wote wawili, pamoja na nia ya kuungana tena na kuliheshimu agano lao la kwanza la ndoa lililobarikiwa na Mungu, si tamaa ya mwili bali ni kazi ya Roho Mtakatifu ndani kabisa ya moyo wa mwenye dhambi. Kunapokuwa na nia ya kumcha Mungu ya kutubu na kupatanisha uhusiano uliovunjika, tunapaswa kupiga magoti tukimwunga mkono na kumshukuru kwa dhati Baba yetu wa Mbinguni.

Yesu amejitolea kuingilia kati na kurejesha mahusiano yenye matatizo ambayo kwa unyenyekevu na toba hutafuta msamaha, na hivyo kurejea katika utumishi kamili kwa Bwana wao na kupata furaha ya milele. Anasema: Kwa maana walipo wawili watatu wamekusanyika kwa jina langu, nami nipo papo hapo katikati yao –Mathayo 18:20. Naye Paulo anasema, Lakini ikiwa Roho yake yeye aliyemfufua Yesu katika wafu anakaa ndani yenu, yeye aliyemfufua Kristo Yesu katika wafu ataihuisha na miili yenu iliyo katika hali ya kufa, kwa Roho wake akaaye ndani yenu –Warumi 8:11.
